Lausanne, January 9, 1930.

VERY IMPORTANT NOTICE.

Fraud involving 1,000,000 French francs
by means of false bills of lading.-------

Messrs. S. E. Kwok and Co., a Chinese firm established
at HHongkong, having accepted offers of paper pulp from
L. O. Baird, a fictitious mill proprietor of Czecho-Slovakia,
giving his address as Lausanne-Ouchy, opened documentary
credits at the Banque Franco-Chinoise for the Industrial
and Commercial Agency of Hongkong for a total of £7988
in favour of L. O. Baird. Upon L. O. Baird producing
to the Paris Branch of the Banque Franco-Chinoise the
bills of lading to show that the goods ordered by Kwok
and Co. had been dispatched by the Ostasiatiske Co. of
Oslo the Bank paid out by cheques a total of £7988 on
the security of the surrender of these documents. The
cheques were cashed at the Union of Swiss Banks at
Lausanne by Baird through the medium of one Cela de Santi,
daughter of Achille and Isabelle nee Pokorni, born on
May 8, 1882 at Venice, native of France, unmarried.

Subsequently it was ascertained that the bills
of lading were false and that the goods had never been
dispatched. It was a case of a new and very clever
method of fraud. A complaint was lodged by the Banque
Franco-Chinoise and the Magistrate of Lausanne commenced
a criminal investigation and issued warrants against:
1) the so-called L. O. Baird and
2) his accomplice Cela de Santi.

The investigations led to the arrest of Cela de
Santi, formerly known under the name of Enrici, at
Tournai, Belgium, on December 14, 1929, and of the
so-called L. O. Baird at Tournai on December 19, 1929.

Baird was identified as Christo Carifalis son
of Jean and Kotore, born on October 22, 1876 or 1877
at Ikaria, Greece, domiciled at Ikaria, a native of
Greece.

When interrogated in prison, Carifalis confessed
to having perpetrated a fraud on the Banque Franco-Chinoise
and acknowledge having cashed a sum of 200,000 Swiss francs
through the woman de Santi, according to the statement of
account of the Union of Swiss Banks.

Carifalis appears to be the same person who,
under the name of Sir John Kerr alias John J. Dennis
alias Xenophon Kallis, resided at Geneva and Lausanne
in 1926 and he very probably was the author of a fraud
perpetrated on the Societe Marseillaise de Credit at
Lausanne. On June 26, 1926 he cashed a forged cheque
for 2220.40 R.M. (?reichmarks) to the order of Frank
R. Hiller drawn by the Amsterdamsche Bank at Rotterdam
on the Darmstadter Bank at Frankfort. The affair at the
time was the subject of criminal investigation at Lausanne
and later in Holland but the offender was never discovered.

-2-

Frank R. Hiller lived at No. II Clarendon
Road, London. During a stay at Vevey in 1926 Kerr gave
his address as Lechorm Road, Harlesdem, N.W. 10.

Carifalis, who used the name of Sir John Kerr
to cash the cheque, cashed another cheque at Geneva
in March 1927 to the order of John J. Dennis endorsed
in blank by the latter. The relation between Kerr
and Dennis is thus established. On the other hand,
Dennis, who is the holder of post office box No. 357 at
the Rive Post Office, Geneva, caused his mail to be
forwarded to the address of Kallis (Post Office Box
Jordils, Lausanne, No. 17613). The wife of de Santi
acknowledged that Baird and Kallis----and consequently
Kerr and Dennis----were one and the same person and
this our investigations have confirmed.

Carifalis appears to be also the same person
as Walther H. Knopper, notified in the Swiss Police
Gazette Article No. 8834 in 1925 by the Police
Department of Bale for a serious case of swindling
perpetrated on Messrs. J. Menasce Fils. of Cairo
and on the Banque d'Industrie at Athens.

At the time of arrest Carifalis was in possession
of the following articles:-
1) A British passport in the name of Charles
Hunter Knox, British, born on July 10, 1877.
2) A British passport in the name of John
Craster, British, born on March 12, 1877.

The following articles were found in a luggage
depot at the Hotel Terminus, Paris:-

3) A British passport in the name of John
Stewart Todd, born on May 19, 1879.
4) A passport, which appears to be genuine, in
the name of Christo Carifalis, Greek.

Carifalis also made use of the following name:
Charles Bellot, No. 19 Aldine Street. He had amongst
his papers a letter-head bearing this name and on which
his profession is given as Solicitor.

Investigations conducted by the London Police
revealed that a boarding house is being maintained at
this address and according to what could be verified
Cela de Santi is known there. She had commissioned the
proprietress of the boarding house to receive all mails
addressed to Bellot and to forward them to the address
of J. A. Craster at Lausanne, Box St. Francis in
envelopes prepared for this purpose.

Later Mrs. Butler whom the London Police describe
as an honest woman but a little simple was informed that
letters addressed to L. O. Baird would reach her and
that she was to hand them to a Mr. Hudson who would call
for them and who in fact did call for them.

Christo Carifalis alias Craster etc. claims to
have an accomplice named Black or Blak residing at this
boarding house who had furnished the false bills of lading
and the false papers of identification. His statements
on this point are rather evasive. Investigations are
proceeding to ascertain whether such a person really
exists or whether he is Carifalis himself. In the
note-book of addresses belonging to Carifalis occurs the
following entry: W. H. Blake, No. 2 Catherine Street,
Dundee, Scotland. This man may have been the accomplice.

-3-

The false documents in the affair of the Banque
Franco-Chinoise were sent by Black to Evian, Postal Box D.
At the time when he cashed the cheques between March, 1929
and November, 1929 Carifalis was living at the Villa Les
Genets, Avenue de la Grande Rive at Evian.

We also noted the names of Knogen and Collins employed
by Carifalis or one of his accomplices when he perpetrated
a swindle under the name of Knopper on Messrs. J. Menasce
of Cairo and on the Banque d'Industrie of Athens. The
following also appeared in his notes: C. Enrici; C. de
Santi, No. 58a Sinclair Road, W. 14. This address was
still that of A. C. Leake-Dawson according to the
note-book of Carifalis and later that of H. Dale-Dawson
according to the printed letter paper and envelopes found
at the home of Carifalis and inscribed as follows:-

H. Dale Dawson,                     86a Sinclair Road,
Exporter.                           London, W. 14.

Carifalis is, without doubt, the author of other
cases of fraud. The investigations have revealed so far
that he has been in correspondence recently with
especially Japan and the following addresses of firms
to which he has made offers of paper etc. have been found:-

The Sumitomo Bank, Ltd., Osaka, Japan.
Sugiyama Co., Ltd. Kiomachibori 2, Osaka.
Jinfound Trading Co.
Hattory Trading Co., Ltd., Ginza Nichome, Tokyo.

One of his principal methods consists of having
a temporary lodging place in various cities throughout
Europe. In this manner, he had false luggage and false
passports to Lille, France, to Metz, Alsace, to Paris etc.
as well as letter boxes at numerous addresses whence
his letters are re-forwarded to his various assumed names.
At the address of Charles Bellot who lives at the
Butler boarding house, 19 Aldine Street, London, we found:

One post box in the name of Craster, St. Francis
Post Office, Lausanne.
One post box No. 17350 in the name of Baird,
Jordils Post Office, Lausanne.
One post box No. 631 in the name of Craster at
Brussels, Belgium.
One address in the name of de Santi, Hotel de
Paris, Tournai.
One box at Paris, Bureau Poste No. 31.
One address R. C., Poste Restante, Prague.
One post box in the name of Baird at Evian.

Besides these there are the old boxes of 1926-1927
in the name of Dennis, Box No. 357 Rive Post Office,
Geneva, and in the name of Kallis, Box No. 17613 Jordils
Post Office at Lausanne. It is probable there are
others and investigations will be made with the object of
determining their existence.

The role played by the woman de Santi appeared to
have been as follows:- At times she is employed by Baird
to secure letters arriving at certain post boxes, and
at other times she is detailed to withdraw the greater
part of funds from the Union of Swiss Banks at Lausanne.

Notifications relating to Carifalis have been issued
as follows:-

On July II, 1925 in article No. 8834 of the Swiss
Police Gazette on Christo Carifalis and Walther H.

-4-
Knopper bythe Police Department of Bale. The article
states that Carifalis is under a warrant of arrest of the
"Landgericht" of Hamburg. According to information
received from the French Criminal Investigation
Department the affair related to a case of fraud
involving 800,000 marks.
2) On November 6, 1925 in article No. II093 of
notifications from Belgium, Christo Carifalis is
mentioned as having been sentenced to seven months
imprisonment plus one month for fraud and for using
a false name.
3) On January 31, 1926 according to notifications
from Germany, Carifalis was wanted on a warrant issued
by Magistrate 7 of Hamburg.

According to information furnished by the French
Criminal Investigation Department when Carifalis
committed a fraud on a firm in Hamburg he was
accompanied by Darlymple, his secretary. At the time of
his arrest at Tournai, Carifalis was in possession of a
receipt issued by the Midland Bank, Ltd., No. 60
Gracechurch Street, London, also in the name of
Darlymple. An investigation was actively commenced to
identify the individual in order to ascertain his
connection with Carifalis.

With the probable object of concealing his funds,
Carifalis had cash deposits in numerous banks amongst
which were the following:-

At the Swiss Bank Corporation, London, No. 99
Gresham Street, about £4600. This money has been
transferred on an order issued by Carifalis from his
prison at Tournai to Messrs. Leader, Plunkett and Leader,
solicitors, No. 49 Newgate Street, London.
At the Banque d'Alsace and de Lorraine, a sum of
235,000 French francs. This money has been sequestrated.
At the Lloyd's National and Provincial Bank, No. 43
Boulevard des Capucines at Paris where a sum of francs 2320
is on deposit in the name of Mrs. Carifalis.
At the London Branch of the Lloyd's National and
Provincial Bank, Lombard Street, where there is a deposit
also in the name of Mrs. Carifalis.
At the Credit Commercial de France, 103 Avenue des
Champs Elysees, a deposit of francs 18,000 in the name
of C. Carifalis.
At the Societe Francais, Brussels, an account in
the name of Craster.
At the Midland Bank, Ltd., Gracechurch Street, a
deposit in the name of Darlymple, 52 Jeffreys Road.
At the Societe de Banque Suisse at Lausanne, a
deposit of 20,000 Swiss francs in the name of Mrs.
Carifalis and another of 1500 Swiss francs in the name of
C. Carifalis were sequestrated.

Carifalis had dealings with other banks, especially
the Banque d'Outremer, Brussels, the Banque Belge Pour
l'Etranger, No. 4 Bishops-gate, E.C. 2, the Banque Federal
at Lausanne and investigations are being made to
ascertain whether there are deposits in any of these
banks. An investigation is also being made to ascertain
whether the fraud committed under the various aliases
had resulted in any transactions with other banks and
whether there are deposits of funds or securities.
Such funds and securities will also be sequestrated.

Little is known of the former life history of
Carifalis. He declares that he was formerly a paper
merchant with offices at No. 3 Tudor Street, London.
Information may be sought at this address which he has

-5-

given as well as from the firm of Whitall in Smyrna where
he has also resided. He states that he has four sons:
Leonidas who is in London (Schools of Economics), Platon
who is on holiday in Paris, Jean and Theodore who are at
present in Greece with the mother. According to the
Belgian notification of 1926, article 11094 we learn that
Theodore Carifalis was born on October 28, 1904 at
Alexandria. On one occasion he was sentenced with his
father to seven months imprisonment for fraud and false
passports. Any information regarding these people and
especially in regard to the places where Theodore
Carifalis has been staying will prove useful because
it is possible his complicity in the present case may
be subsequently established.
    The Chiefs of Police in Switzerland and foreign
countries to whom the present circular is being sent
are kindly requested to institute an active
investigation with the object of ascertaining who
Carifalis is, who are his accomplices and the persons
with whom he has had relations, whether he has committed
any other offences, whether he has any letter boxes
besides those already referred to above.

    Banks to which this circular has been sent
are also requested to make an investigation with the
object of ascertaining whether Carifalis has any
deposits, accounts or safety deposits in any of the
names of which a list is appended or in the names of
members of his family.

Lausanne, January 9, 1930.

VERY IMPORTANT NOTICE.

Fraud involving 1,000,000 French francs
by means of false bills of lading.-------

Messrs. S. E. Kwek and Co., a Chinese firm established
at Hongkong, having accepted offers of paper pulp from
L. O. Baird, a fictitious mill proprietor of Czecho-Slovakia,
giving his address as Lausanne-Ouchy, opened documentary
credits at the Banque Franco-Chinoise for the Industrial
and Commercial Agency of Hongkong for a total of £7988
in favour of L. O. Baird. Upon L. O. Baird producing
to the Paris Branch of the Banque Franco-Chinoise the
bills of lading to show that the goods ordered by Kwek
and Co. had been dispatched by the Ostasiatiska Co. of
Oslo the Bank paid out by cheques a total of £7988 on
the security of the surrender of these documents. The
cheques were cashed at the Union of Swiss Banks at
Lausanne by Baird through the medium of one Cela de Santi,
daughter of Achille and Isabelle nee Pokorni, born on
May 8, 1884 at Venice, native of France, unmarried.

Subsequently it was ascertained that the bills
of lading were false and that the goods had never been
dispatched. It was a case of a new and very clever
method of fraud. A complaint was lodged by the Banque
Franco-Chinoise and the Magistrate of Lausanne commenced
a criminal investigation and issued warrants against:
I) the so-called L. O. Baird and
2) his accomplice Cela de Santi.

The investigations led to the arrest of Cela de
Santi, formerly known under the name of Enrici, at
Tournai, Belgium, on December 14, 1929, and of the
so-called L. O. Baird at Tournai on December 19, 1929.

Baird was identified as Christo Carifalis son
of Jean and Katera, born on October 22, 1876 or 1877
at Ikaria, Greece, domiciled at Ikaria, a native of
Greece.

When interrogated in prison, Carifalis confessed
to having perpetrated a fraud on the Banque Franco-Chinoise
and acknowledge having cashed a sum of 200,000 Swiss francs
through the woman de Santi, according to the statement of
account of the Union of Swiss Banks.

Carifalis appears to be the same person who,
under the name of Sir John Kerr alias John J. Dennis
alias Xenophon Kallis, resided at Geneva and Lausanne
in 1926 and he very probably was the author of a fraud
perpetrated on the Societe Marseillaise de Credit at
Lausanne. On June 26, 1926 he cashed a forged cheque
for 2230.40 R.M. (Reichsmarks) to the order of Frank
R. Hiller drawn by the Amsterdamsche Bank at Rotterdam
on the Darmstadter Bank at Frankfort. The affair at the
time was the subject of criminal investigation at Lausanne
and later in Holland but the offender was never discovered.

-2-

Frank R. Miller lived at No. II Clarendon
Road, London. During a stay at Vevey in 1926 Kerr gave
his address as Lochern Road, Harlesden, N.W. 10.

Carifalis, who used the name of Sir John Kerr
to cash the cheque, cashed another cheque at Geneva
in March 1927 to the order of John J. Dennis endorsed
in blank by the latter. The relation between Kerr
and Dennis is thus established. On the other hand,
Dennis, who is the holder of post office box No. 357 at
the Rive Post Office, Geneva, caused his mail to be
forwarded to the address of Kallis (Post Office Box
Jordils, Lausanne, No. 17613). The wife of de Santi
acknowledged that Baird and Kallis----and consequently
Kerr and Dennis----were one and the same person and
this our investigations have confirmed.

Carifalis appears to be also the same person
as Walther H. Knepper, notified in the Swiss Police

April 22, 1930.

A British stowaway returned to Shanghai from Kobe
on the President Cleveland 18-4-30.

The man concerned, Frank E. Collins, is 18 years
of age, and a native of Sudbury, Ontario, Canada, in
which town he has relatives. Previous to January 1930
he was employed by the International Nickel Company, with
a factory in his home town, as a labourer.

On January 11, 1930, he boarded the "Empress of Asia"
at Vancouver as a stowaway and reached Honolulu where he
lived for about three weeks. His quest for work being
unsuccessful he boarded the freight ship "Stanley Dollar"
as a stowaway, under the impression that the ship was
sailing direct to San Francisco. During this trip, his
presence on board was discovered and he was handed over
to the immigration authorities at Manila, who shipped him
Hongkong where the competent shipping authorities investigated
his case and forthwith returned him to Manila on the
"President Jefferson". Permission for him to land in that
port was refused therefore he was compelled to work his
passage to Shanghai on the same boat. Arriving in this
city, Collins was allowed to land, but a few hours before
the "President Jefferson" sailed, he again stowed away.
During the journey from Shanghai to Kobe his presence on
board was discovered and he was handed over to the authorities
at the latter port. They in turn sent him back to Shanghai
on the "President Cleveland."

Collins is at the present time being cared for at
the Salvation Army Hostel, 2 Tsongchow Road, until
arrangements can be made for his employment locally or until
he can be returned to his native town.
